page: Hetzner Cloud cax31 is an arm64-based virtual server powered by an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 8 physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation. The server is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 1.95 GB of memory per core, and includes 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data shows average performance across several standard workloads. The server achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1740.19 and a multi-core score of 14455.92. Memory bandwidth is measured at 560.18 GB/sec for small block read-only operations and 79.75 GB/sec for large block read-only operations. However, single-core execution is relatively weak, as indicated by a Geekbench single-core score of 1063.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 6189.29. Cryptographic and decompression tasks also show weaker results, with a Passmark CPU encryption score of 1305.95 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 34.03 GB/sec. LLM inference performance is poor to weak, generating 31.49 tokens/sec on a small 135M model.

Given its shared ARM64 architecture, the cax31 offers a resource-dense configuration suitable for cost-conscious deployments. It performs adequately in database operations, scoring 5418.51 on Passmark database tests, and handles static web serving throughput at 8.6 GB/sec. This makes it a viable option for web serving, basic database hosting, software compilation, and general-purpose development workloads that do not require dedicated CPU threads or high-performance single-core execution.
